title: 1994 AHSME Problem 20
statement: Suppose \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z\) is a geometric sequence with common ratio \(r\) and \(x\ne y.\) If \(x,\) \(2y,\) \(3z\) is an arithmetic sequence, then \(r\) is

solutions.text: Because \(y=xr\) and \(z=xr^2,\) the arithmetic-sequence condition gives \[ 4xr=x+3xr^2. \] Here \(x\ne0,\) so \(3r^2-4r+1=0,\) yielding \(r=1\) or \(r=\frac{1}{3}.\) The condition \(x\ne y\) excludes \(r=1,\) leaving \(r=\frac{1}{3}.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
